decisions.context: The brief is for weekly store and product demand forecasts, owned end to end by three data scientists.

chosen.label: Reproducibility first, with safe rapid delivery

decisions.rationale: Reproducing historical forecasts is the top requirement; rapid delivery must not compromise the weekly run.
consequences: Keep the data and model inputs for each run identifiable.

decisions.context: Reproducing a forecast for a past week requires knowing which data was used to train and generate it. The design space compares repository-based versioning with code repository versioning and no versioning (d:11).

alternatives.label: Data version repository
cons: Small team: another tool to operate

alternatives.label: Data versioning in code repository
cons: Small team: repository may not suit large datasets

alternatives.label: No data versioning
cons: Reproducibility: past inputs are hard to recover

decisions.rationale: Reproducing any past week decides the choice: use a dedicated data version repository, accepting the added tool overhead (d:11, v:11.1).
consequences: Record the data version used for each forecast run.

decisions.context: Weekly forecasting suggests a recurring model build, while reproducibility favors repeatable training runs. The design space includes batch, incremental, and hybrid learning (d:19).

alternatives.label: Batch-based learning
cons: Ship model ideas quickly: changes await a run

alternatives.label: Incremental learning
pros: Ship model ideas quickly: update continuously
cons: Reproducibility: harder to reconstruct model state
Protect weekly run: continuous updates add operational risk

alternatives.label: Hybrid batch-based and incremental learning
pros: Ship model ideas quickly: some updates are incremental
cons: Small team: greater operational complexity

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice: batch training makes runs repeatable, at the cost of waiting for the next scheduled run to try a model change (d:19, v:19.1).
consequences: Keep training separate from forecast generation where practical.

decisions.decision: How to trigger the ML pipeline?
decisions.context: The system has a fixed weekly run and needs an efficient path to evaluate new model ideas. The design space includes scheduled and commit-based triggers (d:12).

alternatives.label: On-schedule trigger
cons: Ship model ideas quickly: waits for schedule

alternatives.label: On-commit trigger
pros: Ship model ideas quickly: starts on code or data change
cons: Protect weekly run: changes may contend with scheduled work

alternatives.label: On-demand trigger
pros: Protect weekly run: explicit operator control
cons: Small team: requires manual coordination

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: schedule the recurring pipeline, giving up immediate end-to-end execution on each model change (d:12, v:12.3).
consequences: Provide a separate way to run experiments outside the production schedule.

decisions.decision: How to automate integration and delivery?
decisions.context: A three-person team needs to move model ideas into production without relying on manual deployment steps. The design space compares CI/CD, deployment scripts, and an ML orchestrator (d:8).

alternatives.label: CI/CD pipeline
pros: Ship model ideas quickly: automates delivery
cons: Small team: pipeline setup and maintenance

alternatives.label: Build and Deployment scripts
cons: Ship model ideas quickly: manual deployment remains

alternatives.label: Machine learning orchestrator
pros: Protect weekly run: coordinates multiple pipelines
cons: Small team: added platform complexity

decisions.rationale: Shipping ideas quickly decides the choice: automate integration and delivery, accepting the ongoing effort of maintaining the pipeline (d:8, v:8.1).
consequences: Require checks to pass before delivery.

decisions.context: New model ideas must not break the weekly run, so the pipeline needs checks before production. The design space lists tests for model quality, components, and integration (d:26).

alternatives.label: Testing trained model quality
pros: Protect weekly run: catches degraded forecasts
cons: Ship model ideas quickly: evaluation adds a gate

alternatives.label: Unit testing pipeline components
pros: Ship model ideas quickly: fast component feedback
cons: Protect weekly run: may miss end-to-end failures

alternatives.label: Integration testing pipeline components
pros: Protect weekly run: checks connected components
cons: Ship model ideas quickly: slower feedback

alternatives.label: No testing
cons: Protect weekly run: failures can reach production

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: gate releases on forecast quality, accepting slower delivery while models are evaluated (d:26, v:26.9).
consequences: Define an acceptance threshold for forecast quality.

decisions.decision: How to deploy and recover model versions?
decisions.context: A model change should reach production quickly while allowing recovery if it threatens the weekly run. The design space includes rollback and multiple or single production versions (d:10).

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
pros: Protect weekly run: restore prior model
cons: Small team: preserve and manage deployable versions

alternatives.label: N versions in production
pros: Ship model ideas quickly: run versions side by side
cons: Small team: more production complexity

alternatives.label: Single model in production
cons: Protect weekly run: no explicit recovery path

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: retain a previous deployable model for recovery, at the cost of managing versioned artifacts (d:10, v:10.2).
consequences: Keep the previous model available for redeployment.

uncovered: Storage format and retention for historical forecasts
Forecast accuracy metric and acceptance threshold
Monitoring, alerting, and ownership for failed weekly runs
